completed: V13 migration service/platform/persistence/src/main/resources/db/migration/V13__memory_recall_context_tombstone.sql: new SECURITY DEFINER function recall_memory. No table/privilege-set change; canonical confirmation gate untouched.

recall_memory(owner, relationship_id, conversation_id DEFAULT NULL, max_entries DEFAULT 50): deterministic recall of confirmed memory for ContextPlan injection. Returns ONLY status='ACCEPTED' AND deleted_at IS NULL rows for one owner and one relationship; RELATIONSHIP scope recalled cross-conversation; SESSION scope recalled only when the caller binds the conversation. Source-grouped (RELATIONSHIP before SESSION) and deterministic (ORDER BY scope, created_at, id -- total order via per-owner id), then budget-capped (LIMIT LEAST(GREATEST(max_entries,1),100); the entries upper bound mirrors ContextBudget; exact token budgeting is the runtime consumer's job). Tombstone is structural (deleted_at IS NULL; no vector/matview/cache store to revive from). Cross-owner/cross-relationship -> empty, indistinguishable from an empty relationship (existence hidden, INV-TENANT-001). Unconfirmed/deleted never recalled.

recall_memory is a pure read (no FOR UPDATE, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE); SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path=vc,public; set_config('vc.owner_user_id') before table access; REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC + GRANT vc_api. INV-MEM-001/002 unweakened (recall reads ACCEPTED rows only; never creates candidates or changes status).

A Java recall-to-ContextPlan assembler (calling recall_memory and building ContextEntry(SESSION_MEMORY/RELATIONSHIP_MEMORY) within ContextBudget, with exact token budgeting) is a separate runtime-implementation card; the deterministic SQL read source and its guarantees are complete and verified here.
knownRisks: recall_memory returns owner-scoped memory without checking the relationship belongs to a different active context; it is (owner, relationship_id)-scoped like list_memory/get_memory, so an owner can recall their own memory across their relationships. Same-owner own-data, consistent with the owner-based FORCE RLS model; no cross-tenant leak. The SESSION predicate additionally binds conversation_id, and composite ownership structurally prevents cross-relationship SESSION leakage.

Budget is an entries cap clamped to [1,100], not a token count; exact ContextBudget token budgeting is deferred to the Java consumer (the recall provides a deterministic ordered slice the consumer truncates by tokens).

Recall returns empty (not an error) for foreign/absent ids to hide existence, consistent with the other memory read functions; a future HTTP-facing recall endpoint must preserve that empty-not-404 mapping.
